preamble: Backing and rounding the nucleus of the PRICE diphthong /aɪ/ toward [ɒɪ ~ ɔɪ] is a feature of broad urban and colonial accents of English. In Cockney, /aɪ/ is usually [ɑɪ], but in 'vigorous, dialectal' Cockney it is [ɒɪ] (Wells 1982). Broad Australian English raises and rounds the first element, giving [ɒːe], and Broad New Zealand English retracts and rounds it to [ɒɪ], at times raised further to [ɔɪ]. The rounded variants approach CHOICE without merging with it and are socially stigmatised, so the change stays at the broad end of each accent continuum.

examples.note: Wells gives Cockney PRICE as [ɑɪ], or even [ɒɪ] in broad speech. The vowel can approach CHOICE without fully merging with it.
In broad accents the first element of PRICE is raised and rounded (Wells 1982: 597; Harrington, Cox & Evans 1997).
The first element of /aɪ/ is retracted and rounded in Broad NZE; it approaches CHOICE /oɪ/ without an actual merger, and the rounded variants are stigmatised.

sources: Wells, J. C. (1982). Accents of English. Cambridge University Press. https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511611759
